opl.title: Mechanical Seal Flush (API Plan 11) Verification
opl.purpose: This One Point Lesson explains mechanical seal flush (api plan 11) verification for GA-1201A (HEXANE FEED PUMP) in the HEXANE FEED SYSTEM. Confirm seal flush dP > 1.5 bar before start. Low flush = seal face overheating and hexane leak to atmosphere. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.
safety: Hazard note: this equipment is HIGH CRITICAL handling n-Hexane at up to 16 barg / 80 degC. Observe the following before
and during the task:
Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.

steps.action: Line up discharge flush to seal chamber and open flush isolation
Check PDI-1201 reads 1.5-2.5 bar dP across the flush orifice RO-1201
Verify no visible leak or drip at the gland / seal drain
If dP low, isolate and inspect orifice RO-1201 for plugging by polymer/dirt
Confirm quench (Plan 62) N2/steam is lined up to the outboard side

troubleshooting.symptom: Hexane leak observed at GA-1201A seal gland during operation, seal dr.
troubleshooting.cause: API Plan 11 flush orifice RO-1201 partially plugged causing seal face.
troubleshooting.action: Replaced JC T2100 mechanical seal cartridge, cleaned flush orifice, v.

troubleshooting.symptom: GA-1201A tripped on VSHH-1201 high vibration 7.4 mm/s
troubleshooting.cause: Angular misalignment 0.12 mm/100mm after foundation settlement
troubleshooting.action: Laser re-aligned pump/motor, re-shimmed motor feet, vibration back to.

troubleshooting.symptom: Bearing DE noisy with rising temperature TI-1201 trend
troubleshooting.cause: Outer race spalling on DE bearing due to prolonged misalignment
troubleshooting.action: Renewed DE bearing 7310 BECBM, flushed housing, refilled ISO VG 68

key_learning: Confirm seal flush dP > 1.5 bar before start. Low flush = seal face overheating and hexane leak to atmosphere.
Respect the interlock SEQ-1201: e.g. PSLL-1201 trips at < 0.5 barg - never defeat it without a permit.
Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID; TJC-LLD-PID-1201 before working on GA-1201A.
Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.

opl.title: Minimum Flow Line Operation & Deadhead Protection
opl.purpose: This One Point Lesson explains minimum flow line operation & deadhead protection for GA-1201A (HEXANE FEED PUMP) in the HEXANE FEED SYSTEM. Never run the pump against a closed discharge. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

Do not defeat the min-flow interlock to force higher discharge pressure

opl.title: Vibration Trend Monitoring & Alarm Response (VSHH-1201)
opl.purpose: This One Point Lesson explains vibration trend monitoring & alarm response (vshh-1201) for GA-1201A (HEXANE FEED PUMP) in the HEXANE FEED SYSTEM. A rising vibration trend predicts bearing failure days in advance and lets you plan a repair before a trip. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.
safety: Hazard note: this equipment is HIGH CRITICAL handling n-Hexane at up to 16 barg / 80 degC. Observe the following before
and during the task:
De-energise and isolate the loop; place the function to bypass/inhibit under permit.
Inform the panel operator before working on any trip, valve or transmitter.
Take care with instrument air / hydraulic pressure when disconnecting tubing.
Verify intrinsic-safety / Ex integrity is restored before returning to service.
Wear correct PPE and follow ESD/override control procedures.

steps.action: Record VT-1201 on the daily PdM route in mm/s RMS
Note alarm at 4.5 mm/s and trip at 7.1 mm/s (VSHH-1201)
A rise greater than 1 mm/s within a week = plan a bearing inspection
Correlate the vibration rise with TI-1201 bearing temperature
Escalate to reliability engineer if the 1x running-speed component dominates

troubleshooting.symptom: Scheduled proof test of low-low suction pressure trip
troubleshooting.cause: Switch set-point drift found +0.08 barg during proof test
troubleshooting.action: Recalibrated PSLL-1201 to 0.5 barg trip, function tested to DCS

troubleshooting.symptom: PDI-1201 reading erratic, seal-flush low alarm nuisance-tripping
troubleshooting.cause: Impulse lines fouled with hexane residue/polymer fines
troubleshooting.action: Cleaned impulse lines and re-zeroed PDI-1201 transmitter

troubleshooting.symptom: Discharge flow control hunting, FIC-1201 oscillating
troubleshooting.cause: Loop poorly tuned after transmitter re-range
troubleshooting.action: Re-ranged FT-1201 and retuned FIC-1201 PID parameters

opl.title: Tube-Side Cleaning (Hydrojetting)
opl.purpose: This One Point Lesson explains tube-side cleaning (hydrojetting) for EA-5601 (SOLVENT HEATER) in the SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM. Hexane fouling on the tube side raises the differential pressure (PDT-5605) and cuts the heat duty, leaving cold solvent downstream. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.
safety: Hazard note: this equipment is LOW CRITICAL handling Hexane / MP Steam at up to 16 barg (tube) / 200 degC. Observe
the following before and during the task:
Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.

steps.action: Isolate and drain both sides, then purge with nitrogen
Open the channel cover and remove the old gasket
Hydrojet the tube bores and inspect for pitting/erosion
Verify tube-side dP restored and no residual blockage
Re-gasket with new SW SS316 gasket and box up to torque

troubleshooting.symptom: High tube dP PDT-5605, low solvent outlet temperature
troubleshooting.cause: Hexane fouling / polymer fines deposit on tube bores
troubleshooting.action: Hydrojetted 246 tubes, restored dP and duty, re-gasketed

troubleshooting.symptom: Hexane weep at channel flange
troubleshooting.cause: Spiral-wound channel gasket relaxed / damaged
troubleshooting.action: Renewed channel gasket, re-torqued in cross pattern

troubleshooting.symptom: Continuous steam at condensate, high steam use
troubleshooting.cause: Steam trap element failed open
troubleshooting.action: Replaced steam trap element, verified condensate temperature

key_learning: Hexane fouling on the tube side raises the differential pressure (PDT-5605) and cuts the heat duty, leaving cold solvent downstream.
Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-5601 before working on EA-5601.

opl.title: Thermal-Shock Avoidance on Start-Up
opl.purpose: This One Point Lesson explains thermal-shock avoidance on start-up for EA-5601 (SOLVENT HEATER) in the SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM. Admitting steam onto a cold tube bundle too fast cracks the tube-to-tubesheet joints, causing internal leaks. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.
safety: Hazard note: this equipment is LOW CRITICAL handling Hexane / MP Steam at up to 16 barg (tube) / 200 degC. Observe
the following before and during the task:
Obtain the correct operating permit and brief the shift team before the task.
Confirm hazardous fluids are isolated / inerted as required by procedure.
Beware of flammable, hot, or high-pressure fluids; wear the correct PPE.
Never defeat a safety interlock or trip without an authorised override permit.
Have emergency actions and communications ready before starting.

steps.action: Establish solvent (tube-side) flow first
Admit steam slowly by ramping the TV-5602 / TIC-5602 set-point
Warm the exchanger through gradually
Avoid sudden large steps in the outlet temperature set-point
Watch for knocking that indicates condensate hammer

troubleshooting.symptom: High tube dP PDT-5605, low solvent outlet temperature
troubleshooting.cause: Hexane fouling / polymer fines deposit on tube bores
troubleshooting.action: Hydrojetted 246 tubes, restored dP and duty, re-gasketed

troubleshooting.symptom: Hexane weep at channel flange
troubleshooting.cause: Spiral-wound channel gasket relaxed / damaged
troubleshooting.action: Renewed channel gasket, re-torqued in cross pattern

troubleshooting.symptom: Continuous steam at condensate, high steam use
troubleshooting.cause: Steam trap element failed open
troubleshooting.action: Replaced steam trap element, verified condensate temperature

key_learning: Admitting steam onto a cold tube bundle too fast cracks the tube-to-tubesheet joints, causing internal leaks.
Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-5601 before working on EA-5601.
Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.

opl.title: Tube Leak Detection & Plugging
opl.purpose: This One Point Lesson explains tube leak detection & plugging for EA-5601 (SOLVENT HEATER) in the SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM. A tube leak lets steam into the solvent (rising outlet temperature and water in the solvent); the leaking tube must be found and plugged. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.
safety: Hazard note: this equipment is LOW CRITICAL handling Hexane / MP Steam at up to 16 barg (tube) / 200 degC. Observe
the following before and during the task:
Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.

steps.action: Isolate and hydrotest the shell side to find the leak
Bubble-test to identify the specific leaking tube
Plug both ends of the tube with tapered plugs
Record the plugged-tube count (maximum 5 % of tubes)
Plan bundle replacement if the plugging limit is reached

opl.title: Fouling Trend & Cleaning Schedule (PDT-5605)
opl.purpose: This One Point Lesson explains fouling trend & cleaning schedule (pdt-5605) for EA-5601 (SOLVENT HEATER) in the SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM. Trending the tube-side differential pressure predicts when cleaning is due before the duty is lost. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.
safety: Hazard note: this equipment is LOW CRITICAL handling Hexane / MP Steam at up to 16 barg (tube) / 200 degC. Observe
the following before and during the task:
De-energise and isolate the loop; place the function to bypass/inhibit under permit.
Inform the panel operator before working on any trip, valve or transmitter.
Take care with instrument air / hydraulic pressure when disconnecting tubing.
Verify intrinsic-safety / Ex integrity is restored before returning to service.
Wear correct PPE and follow ESD/override control procedures.

steps.action: Log PDT-5605 differential pressure weekly
Note the PDAH-5605 fouling alarm at 0.7 bar dP
Correlate rising dP with any outlet-temperature shortfall
Plan cleaning before the duty loss becomes critical
Feed the trend into the exchanger cleaning program

troubleshooting.symptom: Outlet temperature hunting around set-point
troubleshooting.cause: Steam valve TV-5602 loop poorly tuned
troubleshooting.action: Retuned TIC-5602 PID, verified stable control

troubleshooting.symptom: Erratic tube dP reading
troubleshooting.cause: Impulse lines plugged with fines
troubleshooting.action: Cleaned and re-zeroed PDT-5605 transmitter

troubleshooting.symptom: Cracked gauge glass on condensate pot
troubleshooting.cause: Thermal/mechanical stress on glass
troubleshooting.action: Replaced LG-5606 gauge glass and seals

key_learning: Trending the tube-side differential pressure predicts when cleaning is due before the duty is lost.
Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-5601 before working on EA-5601.

opl.title: PSV-5607 Testing & Car-Seal Management
opl.purpose: This One Point Lesson explains psv-5607 testing & car-seal management for EA-5601 (SOLVENT HEATER) in the SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM. The tube-side relief valve is the exchanger's overpressure protection and must be proven and never isolated in service. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.
safety: Hazard note: this equipment is LOW CRITICAL handling Hexane / MP Steam at up to 16 barg (tube) / 200 degC. Observe
the following before and during the task:
Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.

steps.action: Confirm PSV-5607 is set to 16 barg on the nameplate
Carry out an off-line pop test per the statutory schedule
Keep the PSV inlet/outlet isolation car-sealed open in service
Record the test certificate and next due date
Never block-in a live PSV without an authorised spare
